selection.objective: Independently discriminate the reported startup loader failure from generic authentication failure.
selection.selectedAction: Z-003 / X-01, using unchanged pinned source and disposable local browser contexts.
selection.reason: Exact-main imported control/intervention report offers high information value and no physical-account cost. Z-002 remains partial provenance debt, not a blocker for source-matched local testing.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Awaited pre-popup work causes loss of transient activation and prevents the Google popup in some environments.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: The popup is invoked and succeeds during the same failing attempt; that attempt must be explained after authentication.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: No activation or popup trace from either physical device. Async code alone does not prove gesture loss.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Connected-account bootstrap failure after Firebase authentication is presented as signed out by the online identity layer.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: A controlled connected=false/bootstrap-error result retains a distinct actionable bootstrap error in the online UI.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: Source supports state collapse; no failing physical account trace. A permanently pending promise is a different mechanism.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Identity startup runs before the optional loader is defined, latches its bootstrap flag and never automatically retries, leaving badge and identity guard absent.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: On unchanged source, firing startup before the loader is ready still automatically recovers after loader availability with no intervention.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: O-05 contains an identity overlay, so absent identity cannot explain every state of Run C; Settings may trigger a later load. Same-device chronology missing.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Continue Career resolves a different or incomplete local/remote authority context and routes into setup despite a preserved existing career.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: The failing synthetic case preserves exact binding and takes the expected canonical resume route; actual failure lies in another boundary.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: Multiple handlers are present, but no observed event conflict or physical deletion trace exists.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Partly populated signing controls have display text but missing canonical selector IDs, triggering client validation before provider mutation.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: At the precise rejection, the client sees valid player text and both valid canonical IDs, and the emitted error demonstrably originates downstream.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: Required text exists in client source. Missing field/ID on physical tablet remains unknown; wording of screenshot wrapper not rechecked.

hypotheses.causalClaim: A retained shell combined with newer network-only assets or a missing versioned resource yields incompatible runtime/UI behavior.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: The relevant loaded asset bytes and cache/controller context match one tested revision during the failure and the failure remains under that coherent runtime.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: P-01 weakens a currently stale public-server sample only; it does not inspect device caches. T-01 offers a coherent-source alternative.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Tablet layout or keyboard constraints make required transfer controls inaccessible, increasing the chance of incomplete input.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: Every required input and action is reachable at the actual measured failing viewport and keyboard state, while rejection persists with valid input.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: Original screenshot and viewport unavailable; generic responsive failure cannot be labelled the original incident.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Reload discards a page-memory private-session capability, and expected reauthorization is mistaken for lost pairing or lost career.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: A valid exact unexpired session is present during failure, or the durable pair/career was actually lost.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: Fresh private session may be required; repeated permanent pairing/setup should not be assumed necessary or acceptable.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Uncommitted transfer draft fields are lost on rerender/reload while provider-committed state survives, producing apparent total progress loss.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: Draft inputs round-trip through an identified persistence path in the failing conditions, or committed state is what is lost instead.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: No complete draft-storage audit yet. Observed UI reset is not proof of local or remote deletion.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Overlapping forced identity initialization or auth callbacks allow an older completion to overwrite newer identity/readiness state.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: Controlled old/new completions cannot publish a state inconsistent with the latest synthetic account generation because all relevant paths reject stale completions.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: Force initialization and multiple callbacks are source facts, not a demonstrated stale-state defect.

hypotheses.causalClaim: Network, runtime configuration, provider quota or permission failures block private bootstrap/session operations after the UI starts.
hypotheses.falsifyingObservation: For the failing boundary, a recorded successful response and valid runtime configuration precede a purely local failure.
hypotheses.remainingUncertainty: No provider logs, deployed Rules readback, incident network trace or safe error codes available.

contradictions.summary: Successful exact-main CI coexists with imported startup failures; timing/coverage differ, so neither cancels the other.
An identity overlay was visible during one attempt; an absent identity module cannot explain that entire attempt without a later load or distinct chronology.
Current source emits the signing text before provider mutation; inherited wording suggests provider error without a response trace.
Original lead asks same-session recovery; current contract intentionally loses capability on reload and may require a fresh exact session for the same rivalry.
POS20 observed refs and NEXT_TASK runtime are stale relative to live refs; they do not set current execution priority.
